text: Students will explore the visual language of drawing in this introductory course. Working primarily from observation, students will develop perceptual and interpretive skills through an exploration of the basic formal elements of line, shape, texture, and tone. (EXP 4) (3 cr)

This course provides a broad introduction to the history of western art from Antiquity to the Middle Ages, the Renaissance, Baroque and Neoclassical eras. The course will cover significant and lesser known works of art and architecture from these periods and will consider how various changes in art reflect and contribute to societal changes. Throughout the course students will be encouraged to develop a critical view of how many of the narratives surrounding cultural production of these periods have contributed to modernist thought, western imperialism and colonial practices. Projects in the course will help you to develop a strong foundation for communicating ideas about art.

metadata.Section header 2: VISA-1406 Introduction to Western Art History

text: This course provides a broad introduction to the history of Eastern art and material culture. Students will be exposed to a wide array of artworks from the Middle East, South Asia, and East Asia from the neolithic to modern era. Throughout the course students will be encouraged to consider ways in which these cultural forms continue to impact contemporary life and projects in the course will help students to develop a strong foundation for communicating ideas about art.

text:
The early 20th century saw unprecedented and radical changes to the forms, conventions, and theoretical underpinnings of visual art. The principles of modernism were also to have a profound effect on literature, music, theatre, architecture, fashion, and virtually every field of human endeavour. This course will introduce the historical background, concepts, and theories of modernism, and will examine how these ideas give rise to new visual forms . Students may not retain credit for VISA-2006 and VISA-2005 . Prerequisites: One of VISA-1206, VISA-1406 or VISA-1407. (LEC 3) (3 cr)

VISA-2007 Late Modern to Postmodern and Contemporary Art This course traces developments in visual art from modern to contemporary art. Contemporary art theory and critical approaches will be studied with a view to understanding the myriad of forms that the visual arts take in the 21st century (such as minimalism, art povera, conceptual art, land-based, installation, and performance art), and will examine how technology and media have influenced both the form and content of visual art. Students may not retain credit for VISA-2007 and VISA-2005 . Prerequisite: One of VISA-1206, VISA-1406 or VISA-1407. It is recommended that students take VISA-2006 prior to VISA-2007. (LEC 3) (3 cr) VISA-2026 Indigenous Futurism, Art + Material Culture of Turtle Island Looking through the lens of Indigenous Futurism, this course introduces the art, stories and material cultures of First Nation, Métis, and Inuit makers; emphasizing the resilience of 500+ nations that live today, in the land that is now

Inuit makers; emphasizing the resilience of 500+ nations that live today, in the land that is now known as Canada. Contemporary works, by FNMI makers from across Turtle Island, taking a range of forms including, images, objects, environments, performances, clothing, films and videos, websites, and texts, will be used as entry points into the work of Indigenous makers, their communities, and cultures, from the past centuries. Through active reading, observation, analysis and critical thinking, students will be asked to make connections between works and reflect on the ways in which Indigenous knowledge continues to pass from generation to generation, into a collective future. a long list of substantial and influential artists. text: In this course students will learn to make pit-fired ceramics from local clay gathered directly from the land. You will learn various methods of hand-building with clay to create vessels and forms including pinch pots, coil building, draped forms, and hand sculpting in addition to an introduction to wheel throwing and finishing the clay surface. All students in the course will be involved in planning for, and preparing fuel for, a pit firing; and will contribute to tending the firing process. Some of the work in the course will contribute to ongoing research projects involving the use of fired clay for soil amendments, the creation of water filters, and more. In addition to gaining plenty of hands-on experience with clay, students will learn about the rich history and traditions of pit-fired ceramics from around the world and artworks that contribute to ecological and social well-being. Prerequisites: VISA-1026, VISA-1027, VISA-1506, or permission of instructor. (LEC/EXP 3) (3 cr)

Topics will include Indigenous expression ( Pre- and Post-contact), confederation and the westward expansion, the Group of Seven, Regionalism and Modernism. text: This part studio, part professional practice based course centres around themes related to Public Art as a Visual art practice. The course will survey contemporary art historical references and present-day examples of Public Art works. It will consider the myriad of ways in which visual artists, and partners can collaborate to create an art work intended for the public realm. You will be required to complete written responses as well as creative visual components, such as maquettes, in relation to the development and actualization of a public art project. Given that public art cannot be created in a silo, much of the course will be centred around communication, collaboration and cultivating partnerships. You will focus on creative problem solving and organisation of ideas as individuals and as a group.
